description: We are a team of Year 10 students passionate about space exploration and coding. For the NASA Space Apps Challenge, we are building the CLPS Lunar Mission Browser—an interactive tool that models solar power availability and Direct-to-Earth communication windows at the Moon's South Pole. We aim to make complex orbital data accessible and showcase the engineering behind lunar exploration.
summary:
Project Orion is an interactive, open-access space data and exploration platform built to bridge the gap between complex orbital telemetry and everyday learners.

What We Developed:

We developed a unified web-based mission console that ingests live NASA open-science feeds, normalizes spatial coordinates, and renders interactive visual trajectory and planetary models—requiring zero registration or technical setup.

How It Addresses the Challenge:

Raw NASA datasets and orbital telemetry are often fragmented across technical archives with steep learning curves. Project Orion consolidates these datasets into an intuitive visual interface where users can select target bodies, toggle live sensor layers, and export mission snapshots in real time.

Why It Is Important:

Democratizing access to space data empowers students, educators, and citizen scientists worldwide to explore and understand our solar system firsthand. By transforming complex telemetry into clear, guided visual storytelling, Project Orion lowers the barrier to entry for STEM education and accelerates global participation in open space science.
details:
Project Orion — Detailed Project Overview

What It Does & How It Works

Project Orion is an interactive, browser-based space exploration and telemetry visualization platform. Users select celestial bodies, satellites, or orbital missions through a clean mission-control interface. Behind the scenes, the platform fetches live datasets from NASA’s Open APIs, normalizes raw spatial and orbital coordinates, and renders real-time interactive 3D/2D trajectory maps alongside guided educational insights. Users can toggle sensor layers, inspect orbital mechanics, and export mission snapshots without needing specialized software.

Key Benefits

  • Zero-Barrier Access: Runs directly in any web browser with no logins, paywalls, or local installations required.
  • Unified Data Stream: Eliminates the need to navigate dozens of disconnected mission archives by consolidating telemetry into a single visual workspace.
  • Guided Discovery: Translates complex astronomical numbers into intuitive, visual narratives suitable for both classrooms and independent learners.

Intended Impact

Project Orion aims to democratize space science by turning passive observers into active explorers. By making authentic NASA mission data immediately understandable and interactive, it supports STEM educators, inspires students worldwide, and accelerates citizen-science engagement.

Tools, Languages, Hardware & Software Used

  • Frontend & Visualization: HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript (ES6+), WebGL / Three.js for spatial and orbital rendering.
  • Data & Backend: Python / Node.js for API aggregation and coordinate normalization, integrated with NASA Open APIs (such as NASA Exoplanet Archive, Horizons, and Earth Observatory feeds).
  • Hosting & Collaboration: Google Sites / GitHub for public deployment, Figma for UI/UX mission-console prototyping, and standard developer laptops.

Creativity & Innovation

Rather than presenting space data as static tables or dense scientific charts, Project Orion reimagines public telemetry as a tactile "Mission Control" experience—blending real-time scientific accuracy with approachable, story-driven visual design.

Key Factors Considered by Our Team

  • Accessibility & Performance: Designed to load smoothly on standard school or home hardware with clear visual contrast and intuitive controls.
  • Data Reliability: Built modular API handlers to gracefully manage rate limits and keep orbital trajectories accurate.
  • User Experience: Prioritized clarity over clutter so first-time users can grasp orbital concepts within seconds.
